statement: The pinned WiiBrew Wiimote Data Reporting introduction describes report mode 0x30 (core buttons) as the startup default and output report 0x12 as the host's mode-selection mechanism. Only report modes carrying accelerometer data also embed its low-order bits in otherwise unused core-button bit positions. In the interleaved modes 0x3E and 0x3F, the interleaved core-button bytes instead carry Z-axis acceleration data; they do not carry the usual low-order accelerometer fragments. After an extension attachment change, the host must reselect a report mode to resume data reporting. These are historical community-protocol descriptions, not measurements of hardware cadence.

applicability.revision: WiiBrew community documentation, no model-specific retail hardware capture
applicability.scope: WiiBrew Wiimote oldid 123257, Data Reporting introductory paragraph (mode 0x30 default, 0x12 selection, only acceleration-bearing modes embed LSBs, interleaved 0x3E/0x3F button bytes carry Z-axis accelerometer data), plus the 0x3E/0x3F section.
